thread:
kai: FYI seeing canary % jump in prod dashboards even though rollout shows 5% in console.
maria: which metric? overall requests or routed count? :thinking:
kai: routed_count. Console rollout UI shows 5% but our router's guard escalated and temporarily bumped canary for a subset. logs attached below.
jen: did the hash/routing change recently? any header-based overrides?
kai: no config change. quick dump of the router decision log:
```
[2025-08-14T18:13:02Z] route-check user=uid:12345 route=service-a guard=evaluate -> bucket=canary seed=0x9ab3 sampled=true
[2025-08-14T18:13:02Z] route-check user=uid:67890 route=service-a guard=evaluate -> bucket=control seed=0x4f12 sampled=false
```
kai: note the boolean `sampled` comes from our telemetry sampler, and the guard uses sampled_count/window to decide whether to open the guard for more traffic.
ryan: wait we're using sampled counts in the guard decision? that sounds off — the guard should use actual routed counts from the router, not metrics post-sampling.
maria: yep. Looks like telemetry sampling rate was 0.1 in us-west and 1.0 in eu-west for a short window due to a deploy of the metrics agent.
jen: so the guard thought control traffic volume was lower (because it was dropped by sampler) and increased canary to compensate -> perceived canary surge.
kai: exactly. That caused sticky sessions to flip because some users were suddenly put into canary variant and their `session_id` cookies were tied to the old bucket; results in mixed session state and quota fallbacks for a small %.
ryan: can we reproduce locally? what's the config snippet?
```
# metrics-agent.yaml
sampling:
  default: 0.1
  overrides:
    eu-west-1: 1.0
```
maria: that override was accidentally pushed in the agent PR (cc @jen for review flow). It ran for ~3m before rollback.
jen: oof. two steps: 1) patch guard logic to rely on router counters (absolute routed tokens) for rollout decisions, 2) console should show both sampled and routed counts so PMs stop being misled.
kai: also propose a quick hotfix: when guard sees sampling_rate variance > 2x across regions, treat metrics as unreliable and fall back to configured rollout ratio rather than dynamic escalation.
ryan: agreed. I'll open a tiny change: router exposes `routed_count` metric to the guard endpoint and we'll add a config flag `guard.use_routed_counts` default true.
maria: I'll file an incident note and ping oncall so customer-facing teams know about the ~0.7% user impact window (small but visible in logs).
deploy-bot: Deployment started: ryan/guard-use-routed-counts -> canary (1 instance)
jen: also UX item: console should display a small tooltip "uses sampled telemetry; counts may differ from routed requests" when sampling is enabled.
kai: thanks team. action items: ryan PR (guard fix), jen UX tweak, maria incident blurb + postmortem, kai follow up to ensure cookie stickiness tests added to rollout e2e.
ryan: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/eng-platform/pulls/4387
maria: incident update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/246
kai: closing the loop — telemetry agent fix + rollback removed the sampling override. watch for any further drift in the next 24h. :thumbsup:
